_notes: FULL-COVERAGE DUMMY 1099-DIV — every one of the 72 writable boxes on Drake's DIV
screen carries a value, so one run proves the whole map at once. The only box left
out is field 13, the payer's foreign province, which is a '<Click to Access>'
sub-screen and not typeable at all.
The amounts are deliberately distinct and nothing like a real statement — 1000, 1100,
2000, 2100 ... — so every box on the screenshot can be traced back to the field that
wrote it. This is a TEST RETURN payload. It is not anybody's tax data.
THIS SCREEN HAS FOUR COLUMNS. Boxes 1a/1b/2a appear under Total, Foreign Amount,
Foreign Percent AND Nominee Amount, and 2b/2c/2d repeat under Nominee. So Box 1a is
four different field numbers (18, 43, 47, 51) and they are not adjacent. The amounts
here are staged by column — 1000s are Totals, 1900s are Foreign Amounts, small numbers
are percents, 3000s are Nominee — so a value in the wrong column is obvious by eye.
Drake expects the Foreign Amount OR the Foreign Percent on a row, not both. Both are
sent here ON PURPOSE: this is a coverage run whose job is to prove every box can be
written, and no real return should ever be sent this way. Same for the three
amount/percent pairs at 60-65.
The country boxes (14, 32) take an IRS country code, NOT ISO 3166 — Drake's own list,
read out of the control on 2026-08-12, has Australia as AS and Austria as AU. 'CA' is
Canada in that list and there is no California in it.
box2c_section_1202_type is 'Q1'. Drake offers exactly Q1, Q3 and Q4 — there is no Q2.
On a real return this is a preparer's determination from WHEN the stock was acquired,
which a 1099-DIV does not print, so it should never come from an extraction.
ALL TEN DROPDOWNS ARE NOW CONFIRMED — the live run on 2026-08-12 read every one of
them back off the form, and fields 32 and 71 echoed the entry Drake selected ('CA
Canada', 'A A'). They still carry the verify-by-eye flag: a dropdown with no matching
entry accepts the typing, echoes it in the popup and stores NOTHING, so the per-field
gate can pass while the box stays empty, and only the form check catches that.
Client: the test return 123456789 / fynn, Test.
federal_code is '0' because that is the only thing Drake accepts in that box besides
blank ('0' excludes the item from the federal return). On a real return nobody should
be setting it from an extraction — it is a preparer's election. It is here so the box
is proven, on a test return where excluding the item costs nothing.
